summary: Baileys fork covertly auto-follows author-controlled WhatsApp newsletters using installer's session
details: The package presents as a drop-in Baileys fork. Inside makeWASocket(), a setTimeout runs ~90 seconds after init, decodes a base64-obfuscated URL (https://main.bwmxmd.co.ke/xmd.json), fetches a JSON list of WhatsApp JIDs, and issues 'follow newsletter' mex queries against each JID using the installer's authenticated WhatsApp session. The destination is not a plain literal — it is reconstructed from Buffer.from(<base64>,'base64').toString() to hide it from static inspection. The list of followed accounts is author-controlled and can be rotated at any time without a package update. No user opt-in, no documentation of this behavior. There is no credential exfiltration, no RCE, no filesystem persistence — the covert action is limited to reach/subscriber padding for author-chosen targets using the installer's identity.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
